subject.title: feat(codex): fork upstream-linked sessions at a message via thread/fork

question: Should OpenClaw commit to `AgentHarness.sessionFork` and plugin-accessible upstream-link mutation as stable generic plugin-SDK contracts, rather than keeping the Codex follow-up behind a narrower owner-approved seam?
rationale: The PR intentionally expands exported plugin APIs and persistence mutation authority; tests can validate mechanics but cannot establish the permanent cross-plugin contract or its ownership boundary.

options.title: Approve the generic SDK contract
options.body: Confirm this is a supported cross-harness API, then require the binding repair, compatibility coverage, and live final-head proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the contract first
options.body: Keep the Codex behavior behind a smaller owner-specific or generic internal seam until a broader harness-fork use case is approved.

recommendation.title: Approve the generic SDK contract
recommendation.body: Confirm this is a supported cross-harness API, then require the binding repair, compatibility coverage, and live final-head proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged session-fork feature and this proposed generic Codex follow-up, making them the strongest available routing candidate for clarifying the intended contract.
